Title: Thousands await aid after Indonesia quake kills 51
Article:
RUTENG, Indonesia: Help started arriving Sunday for thousands of evacuees on Indonesia's Flores island after a powerful earthquake killed 51 people, injured dozens and damaged hundreds of houses and buildings.
Some 5,000 people fled their homes as the 7.7-magnitude quake hit the island early Saturday, followed by at least 341 aftershocks in the hours that followed, a spokesman for the BNPB national disaster agency, Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan, said.
People in some areas were left without electricity and telecommunications and at least one emergency access road remained inaccessible.
"We need food, drink, medicines, and diapers for the children," Umri, a resident of Nangahale village on the north coast of Flores, told AFP on Sunday morning.
The 55-year-old, who like many Indonesians uses one name, has been hiding out on a hilltop for 24 hours with others afraid to return home.
Nurhidayati, also 55, spent the night on a mat on the same hill.
"I'm still terrified; my heart is pounding hard remembering yesterday's tremor... We just ran up here yesterday. I'm very scared now, still traumatised by the quake in 1992. I don't dare to go home," she said.
Flores was struck by a 7.7-magnitude earthquake in 1992 that triggered a tsunami and killed about 2,500 people.
"I hope the government will soon distribute logistics to help us," said Nurhidayati.
BNPB head Suharyanto said Sunday at least five helicopters, several planes, a naval vessel and search and rescue ships were were on their way to help.
- EMERGENCY RESPONSE -
The National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) said Sunday the death toll had risen to 51 from 47 the day before.
Another 132 people were injured, with no reports of missing persons.
Survivors were in urgent need of assistance in the form of emergency tents, food, medicines, blankets, camp beds, mats, clean water and electricity generators.
The epicentre of the shallow quake was located just off the north coast of the island, geological authorities said.
The affected areas have few, if any, high-rise buildings.
Berton said at least 914 houses were severely damaged and hundreds of others to a lesser degree.
Dozens of public facilities were also stricken, including 93 educational and 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said Saturday preparations were under way to bring aid to thousands in temporary shelters.
The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc's Copernicus Earth observation satellites.
"Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you," she wrote on X.
- 'RING OF FIRE' -
In Ruteng, a town about 200km from the worst-hit part of the island, AFP saw heavy machinery clearing rubble from the street Sunday.
Yohana Raisita Damalia Mari, a spokeswoman for the local hospital, said the building had been badly damaged, and patients were evacuated to tents erected outside.
A woman underwent an emergency C-section in an intact storage room converted into a temporary operating theatre.
"Thank God, the surgery went smoothly and both the patient and her baby are safe," said Yohana.
Herybertus Geradus Laju Nabit, mayor of the Manggarai regency, told AFP it was impossible to predict when the aftershocks would end.
"Therefore, our first appeal is: be vigilant. Stay alert," he said.
After Saturday's quake, Flores residents ran for the hills as the sea retreated, a possible sign of an approaching tsunami.
A tsunami warning was later lifted, but authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.
Waves of up to 1.6m were reported in some coastal regions, according to Indonesia's BMKG geological agency.
Indonesia experiences frequent earthquakes due to its location in the Pacific "Ring of Fire", an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
A devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 struck off the coast of Sumatra and triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 throughout the region, about 170,000 of them in Indonesia.
It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.--AFP

Title: Malaysia braces for stronger El Nino, worsening transboundary haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government is bracing for a stronger El Nino and the possibility of a more severe wave of transboundary haze as prolonged hot and dry conditions increase the risk of fires across the region.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the phenomenon was intensifying alongside the southwest monsoon, resulting in reduced rainfall and hotter, drier weather.
He said the ministry was taking seriously the haze situation that has affected Sarawak, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya since Aug 8. However, he said conditions in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya had improved.
"As of noon today, haze conditions nationwide showed three areas in Sarawak, namely Kuching, Samarahan and the Serian district police headquarters, as well as Johan Setia in Peninsular Malaysia, recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"The remaining areas recorded moderate API readings," he said in a statement today.
Kurup said preparations to deal with El Nino and the southwest monsoon had begun in June, when the National Haze and Dry Weather Committee held its first meeting of the year on June 15.
"State governments and other agencies had been briefed on the implications of El Nino for agriculture, water supply and reservoirs, as well as the increased risk of open burning and haze.
"Measures would be implemented in accordance with the National Haze Action Plan and the National Open Burning Action Plan," he said.
Kurup said Malaysia had also raised the issue at the 27th Ministerial Steering Committee and Technical Working Group meetings on transboundary haze pollution in Bali, Indonesia, on July 8 and 9.
"The meetings involved Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste, with participating countries presenting their respective strategies and initiatives to prevent forest and land fires," he said.
Kurup said he also held bilateral discussions with Indonesia's Environment Minister and delegation during the meetings, during which both countries exchanged views and coordinated efforts to monitor and curb an increase in hotspots.
He said the ministry also participated in the 37th Meeting of the Asean Senior Officials on the Environment from Aug 10 to 13, where the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre forecast stronger El Nino conditions than in 2025 and a prolonged dry period, increasing the risk of transboundary haze.
Kurup said the ministry had planned several measures in response, including sending an official letter to the Asean Secretariat urging countries in the region to intensify efforts and maintain continuous preparedness for a stronger El Nino and possible worsening transboundary haze.
"Under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, Alert Level 2 was activated on Aug 3.
"Countries in southern Asean are required to submit daily reports and immediate notifications on fires, haze conditions and measures taken," Kurup said.

Title: Sara to continue despite country facing current global economic challenges – Amir Hamzah
Article:
TAWAU: Efforts to provide assistance to the people through the Basic Rahmah Contribution (Sara) programme remain the government's priority in preparing the 2027 Budget despite the current challenging global economic environment, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the government through the budget would continue to provide allocation space for the targeted cash assistance programme next year to ease the burden of the people's cost of living, especially the needy.
"This effort is effective in helping those who may not have enough to meet the cost of living, so this is one of our priorities.
"In terms of how the government controls spending, it is an important matter through the implementation of targeted subsidies to increase the space for more effective programmes for the people and local entrepreneurs," he said.
He told reporters after reviewing the implementation of the Sara programme at a supermarket here today.
Amir Hamzah said the Sara programme has proven effective as the total allocation for Sara and the Rahmah Cash Contribution this year reached RM15 billion.
"Almost nine million Sara recipients with 99 per cent benefiting from it, thus proving that this programme truly reaches the target group at the grassroots level," he said.
Meanwhile, he said the Malaysian economy remained on a strong growth path despite facing uncertainties in the geopolitical and global economic situation.
He explained that the country's economic resilience was driven by the good reception of local export products as well as the stability of the domestic economic engine through spending consumers and investment inflows that remain competitive.
"This situation supports economic growth with the unemployment rate remaining low below three percent in addition to the inflation rate being controlled at 1.9 per cent through effective action plan initiatives," he said.
According to him, the implementation of the Madani Economic framework has proven to be successful in continuously catalysing the growth of the country's gross domestic product (GDP).
"Last year, the country's GDP growth recorded 5.2 per cent while for the first quarter of 2026 we recorded 5.4 per cent and increased to 6.0 per cent in the second quarter, making the average growth so far 5.7 per cent," he said.

Title: Jakarta team to brief NCID top brass this week on pilot drug case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Bukit Aman team sent to Jakarta to interview a Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in a major drug trafficking case will brief the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) top brass this week on leads uncovered during three days of questioning.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team returned to Malaysia on Saturday (Aug 15) after interviewing the 39-year-old pilot in Jakarta from Aug 12 to 14.
He said the officers would rest over the weekend before presenting their findings to the department's senior leadership.
"We need a bit more time to follow up on all the leads the team has uncovered.
"It's not just a question of diving straight into catching the syndicate members. We need to conduct cross-checks and verification before we can act on these leads," he told the New Straits Times.
Hussein said investigators were also seeking to establish the full extent of the suspect's alleged activities, including how long he had been involved and how many countries he may have smuggled drugs to.
"We urge the public to be patient so we can conduct our investigation carefully and completely dismantle the Malaysian side of this syndicate," he said.
The NCID team travelled to Jakarta on Aug 11 with the cooperation of Indonesian police to interview the pilot, who was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28.
The Malaysian officers were initially scheduled to interview him on Aug 12 and 13, but Indonesian authorities allowed the sessions to be extended by another day until Aug 14.
Hussein had earlier said the interviews yielded information on syndicates operating in Malaysia and overseas, as well as individuals allegedly linked to domestic and international drug trafficking networks.
The 39-year-old suspect
was travelling on Malaysia Airlines flight
MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta when he was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport on July 28 with
70,000 ecstasy pills
.
He also tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine after landing in Jakarta.
Preliminary investigations found that the suspect admitted he had been instructed by an individual to transport the drugs to Jakarta in exchange for RM50,000.
He told investigators that upon arriving in Jakarta, he would be directed by someone believed to be based in Malaysia, while another person would collect the drugs at a hotel or accommodation.
The suspect also told investigators that he had acted as a drug courier three times.

Title: Merdeka Month: Taking responsibility for our future
Article:
LETTER:
Every August, Malaysians proudly celebrate Merdeka Month, a time when we commemorate our nation's independence and pay tribute to the sacrifices of our founding fathers and all those who fought tirelessly to secure our freedom.
However, Merdeka Month should be much more than displaying the Jalur Gemilang, attending parades, and participating in patriotic events.
It should be a time for deep reflection on the true meaning of independence and our collective responsibility to safeguard and strengthen the nation for future generations.
As Malaysia approaches another National Day, we must ask ourselves an important question: What does Merdeka mean to Malaysians today?
Political independence, achieved in 1957, gave us the right to govern ourselves. Yet true independence goes beyond political freedom. It also means freedom from poverty, corruption, ignorance, discrimination, injustice, extremism, hatred and fear.
It means creating a society where every Malaysian has equal opportunities to succeed regardless of race, religion or background.
Today, Malaysia faces many new challenges. Economic uncertainties, rising cost of living, climate change, rapid technological transformation, misinformation, cyber threats, mental health issues, and increasing social polarisation are testing our resilience as a nation.
These challenges cannot be overcome by the government alone. They require the active participation of every citizen.
Merdeka Month reminds us that nation-building is a continuous journey. Independence is not a destination but an ongoing commitment to improve ourselves and our country.
The government has an important role to play. It must continue strengthening good governance, uphold integrity, ensure transparency and accountability, promote inclusive economic growth, improve education and healthcare, protect the environment, and create opportunities for young Malaysians to thrive.
Policies must be people-centred and future-oriented so that no one is left behind. At the same time, the people also have responsibilities. Patriotism should not be expressed only through words but through daily actions.
Respecting the law, paying taxes honestly, protecting public property, volunteering in the community, helping those in need, practising moderation, rejecting corruption, and respecting our diversity are all expressions of genuine love for our country.
Parents and educators have a particularly important role in nurturing patriotism among the younger generation.
Our children should understand not only the historical events leading to independence but also the values that made nation-building possible — unity, mutual respect, tolerance, hard work, integrity, and service to others.
In today's digital age, patriotism also means being responsible users of social media. Malaysians should reject fake news, avoid spreading hatred and misinformation, and instead promote respectful dialogue and national unity.
Our words and actions, whether online or offline, can either strengthen or weaken the fabric of our society.
The spirit of the Rukun Negara should remain our moral compass. Its principles continue to provide a strong foundation for national harmony, responsible citizenship, and social cohesion. More than five decades after its introduction, its message remains as relevant as ever.
Merdeka Month should also inspire us to become better citizens. A developed nation is not measured solely by its infrastructure or economic achievements, but by the character of its people — their civic-mindedness, integrity, compassion, discipline, and willingness to work together for the common good.
As we celebrate our independence this August, let us remember that the future of Malaysia lies not only in the hands of our leaders but also in the hearts and actions of every Malaysian.
Let this Merdeka Month renew our commitment to building a nation that is united in diversity, strong in integrity, compassionate in spirit, and confident in facing the future.
Our greatest tribute to the generation that won our independence is not merely to celebrate their achievements, but to ensure that the Malaysia we leave behind for our children is even stronger, more united, and more prosperous than the one we inherited.
Merdeka is not only about remembering our past — it is about taking responsibility for our future.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Unity Advocate
Kuala Lumpur
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: USM leaps 149 places to lead Malaysia in global university ranking
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has emerged as Malaysia's top university in the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2026.
USM climbed 149 places to No 581 globally from No 730 in 2025, while rising from third to first nationally.
Also known as the ShanghaiRanking, ARWU evaluates universities based on academic and research performance rather than reputation or perception alone.
Its indicators include alumni and staff who have won Nobel Prizes and Fields Medals, Highly Cited Researchers  recognised by Clarivate, papers published in Nature and Science, publications indexed in the Science Citation Index-Expanded and Social Sciences Citation Index, as well as per-capita academic performance.
Nobel Prize and Fields Medal laureates account for 30 per cent of the assessment, while Highly Cited Researchers contribute another 20 per cent.
"As an APEX University, we will continue to strengthen research excellence, nurture world-class researchers and generate knowledge capable of creating global impact," USM said today.
More than 2,500 universities worldwide are evaluated annually, with only the top 1,000 published in the ranking.
In ARWU 2026, USM ranked No 424 globally for the Publication indicator, reflecting its strength in producing research recognised in major international databases.
Its performance in the Highly Cited Researchers indicator also improved to No 503 globally.
According to USM, its rise from No 730 to No 581 globally, coupled with its move from No 3 to No 1 in Malaysia, reflects continued strengthening of its research ecosystem.
"The performance also points to progress in high-quality publications, research impact and citations, the development of high-performing researchers and academic productivity," it added.

Title: 12 killed as Polish bus overturns in Hungary
Article:
BUDAPEST: A Polish bus overturned on a Hungarian highway early Sunday killing 12 people and leaving at least 10 with serious injuries, Prime Minister Peter Magyar and officials said.
The coach, heading from Serbia to Poland, crashed at 1am (2300 GMT Saturday) on the M3 highway near Mezokeresztes, east of Budapest, according to a police statement.
The bus, with 57 passengers and two drivers, "left the road, ended up in a ditch, and came to a stop on its side," the national disaster management agency said in a social media post.
Eleven people were declared dead at the scene and another person died in hospital, the agency said. The ambulance service said 37 people suffered minor injuries.
The fire brigade and other rescuers had to drag some people out through the windows because they were trapped in the bus. Two cranes eventually lifted the bus out of the ditch, according to the disaster management agency.
It is the worst road accident in Hungary since a train hit a German tourist bus at Siofok in 2003, killing 33 people. In 2002, a bus carrying Polish pilgrims crashed near the western town of Balatonszentgyorgy (ouest) killing 19 people.
Magyar announced the death toll of the latest disaster on social media.
"I send my sincere condolences to the families of the victims," he said. "I thank all the people who took part in the rescue operation."
Poland's Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski called it a "tragic bus accident involving Polish tourists" in a post on X. "The consular service is acting. We are in contact with the Hungarian authorities," he added. Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed there were 12 dead.--AFP

Title: Businessman's body found in net: One suspect also faces firearms charge
Article:
BATU PAHAT: One of
four suspects
who will be charged tomorrow over the alleged murder of a businessman whose body was found wrapped in a net is also facing a firearms possession charge.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a pistol was found at a house in Yong Peng following the arrest of two suspects, aged 33 and 34, on Aug 4.
"So far, five suspects have been detained and four will be charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
"One of the suspects will also be charged under Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971.
"Meanwhile, another suspect was released on bail under Section 118 of the Criminal Procedure Code and will be called as a prosecution witness," he said in a statement.
Ab Rahaman said checks found that one of the two suspects had a previous criminal record.
He added that preliminary urine screening tests on the suspects were negative for prohibited substances.
He said the charges under Section 302 would be heard at the Batu Pahat magistrate's court, while the firearms possession charge would be heard at the Kluang Sessions Court.
Both proceedings will be held tomorrow.
Earlier today, it was reported that police had received a directive from the Johor State Legal Adviser's Office to prosecute the suspects.
It was previously reported that the body of a 39-year-old man was found bound and wrapped in netting in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, near here, early this month.
Preliminary investigations found that the victim was allegedly strangled with a rope before his hands were bound with adhesive tape and his body wrapped in a net.
Police also found five stones on the body, believed to have been used to weigh it down and prevent it from resurfacing.
The discovery ended the mystery surrounding the disappearance of the businessman, who was reported missing from Mutiara Rini, Iskandar Puteri, on July 29.
The victim was identified by his next-of-kin based on the clothing and personal belongings found with the body.

Title: Weather warning: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit 10 states and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until 6pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the affected areas include Perlis; Kedah (Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Kota Setar, Sik, Baling and Pendang); and Perak (Hulu Perak).
The warning also covers Kelantan (Gua Musang); Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, Marang and Kuala Terengganu); Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Bera, Rompin, Pekan and Jerantut); and Selangor (Hulu Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Gombak and Kuala Langat).
Similar weather conditions are expected in Negri Sembilan (Jempol, Tampin, Seremban, Kuala Pilah, Jelebu and Rembau), Johor (Segamat, Kota Tinggi and Mersing), and Sarawak (Miri, Marudi and Limbang).

Title: Pas open to seat swaps with Umno in upcoming elections
Article:
TEMERLOH: Pas is prepared to consider swapping its incumbent state and parliamentary seats with Umno, subject to certain conditions in upcoming elections, deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said.
He said, in principle, incumbent seats should remain with the party that won them in the previous general election, but seat swaps could be considered through negotiations based on circumstances in each constituency.
"For example, Umno might want to contest a particular seat, but they may have to give up another seat of equal standing. Any proposed seat exchange should generally involve a 'win seat for win seat' or 'losing seat' arrangement.
"Negotiations are not necessarily limited to seats within the same state or parliamentary constituency but could involve constituencies across different states," he told reporters after opening the national-level cyber troopers' or 'mujahid cyber' convention at the party's Al Makmur Complex here today.
Tuan Ibrahim said Pas was flexible in determining the most suitable arrangements through negotiations, given the people's positive response to efforts towards 'penyatuan ummah' (Muslim unity).
Earlier, Tuan Ibrahim was asked whether Pas planned to maintain the status quo by defending all the state seats it currently holds, including those in Pahang, in the upcoming elections.
On seat negotiations to establish political cooperation with Pahang Umno, Tuan Ibrahim said it was still too early to discuss the matter as the focus was currently on the Melaka state election.
"I believe all parties are focusing on the Melaka state election, followed by Sarawak, and let's see what happens after that," he said.
Last week, Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said the party was ready for talks.
Pahang Umno liaison chief Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail subsequently said Umno was open to cooperating with any political party, including Pas.

Title: Malaysia's growth forecasts lifted after stronger Q2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several research firms have raised their forecasts for Malaysia's 2026 economic growth after the economy expanded faster than expected in the second quarter (Q2).
Malaysia's gross domestic product expanded six per cent in Q2, accelerating from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter and exceeding both Bloomberg consensus expectations and the Statistics Department's advance estimate of 5.8 per cent.
The stronger growth was driven by higher growth in the services and manufacturing sectors, a rebound in mining output and stronger domestic spending.
The economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half (H1) of 2026.
Kenanga Research raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.5-5.0 per cent, while MBSB Research lifted its projection to 5.1 per cent from 4.5 per cent.
Meanwhile, RHB Research maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.4 per cent, above the government's official projection of 4.0-4.5 per cent and Bank Negara Malaysia's forecast range of 4.0 to 5.0 per cent.
JPMorgan had earlier raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 5.0 per cent on July 21, following the stronger-than-expected Q2 advance estimate.
Kenanga Research said its new forecast implied growth of around five per cent in the second half (H2), allowing for some moderation from the strong Q2 momentum as frontloading effects fade.
"Pickup in private consumption, continued services expansion and ongoing public and private investment are expected to support growth," it said.
The firm said private consumption should benefit from stable employment, sustained wage growth and targeted government assistance.
The electrical and electronics (E&E) sector should continue to gain from structural demand linked to digitalisation, artificial intelligence and the broader global technology cycle.
However, it flagged geopolitical uncertainty, tariff-related frictions and commodity price volatility as key external risks.
MBSB Research said the stronger quarterly performance was mainly supported by a pickup in external trade, particularly strong demand for E&E and petroleum products.
"Overall, we expect the continued rise in domestic demand would continue to anchor Malaysia's sustainable economic growth, underpinned by increased tourism activity and higher income with inflation remained generally under control," it said.
Nevertheless, MBSB Research expects growth momentum to slow in H2 due to fading base effects, supply disruptions and higher cost pressures.
It also warned that Malaysia's open economy remains exposed to geopolitical tensions, prolonged trade and supply disruptions, higher inflation, tighter trade rules and potentially weaker final demand.
RHB Research said its autoregression and leading economic index models pointed to sustained growth of between 5.0 per cent and 5.2 per cent in H2.
"The robust H1 2026 growth of 5.7 per cent, together with today's stronger-than-expected 6.0 per cent growth reading, further reinforces our constructive view," it said.
RHB Research expects resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in E&E exports to support growth for the remainder of the year.
It said Malaysia remained relatively well-positioned to navigate external challenges, supported by its diversified economic structure, deep integration into regional and global supply chains, and efforts to diversify export markets and expand its product offerings.
RHB Research, however, warned that a prolonged escalation in geopolitical tensions could weigh on the outlook.
Under its worst-case scenario, disruptions to oil infrastructure could push Brent crude prices as high as US$140 a barrel, weakening global trade and raising production costs.
In such a scenario, Malaysia's GDP growth could slow to 4.6 per cent, 0.8 percentage points below its baseline forecast.
Despite the stronger growth outlook, Kenanga Research and RHB Research expect the central bank to keep the overnight policy rate at 2.75 per cent for the remainder of 2026.
Kenanga Research said there was limited justification for monetary policy tightening as inflationary pressures remained manageable.
"The current monetary policy setting still looks appropriate, as growth has picked up without broad-based demand-side inflation.
"Risk remains largely supply-driven, and targeted government support measures should help cushion the impact on households," it said.
RHB Research said monetary policy would remain data-dependent, with a 25-basis-point hike possible if inflation became higher and more volatile than expected.
"The current economic environment and inflation trajectory support a broadly stable policy outlook, with no immediate pressure for rate adjustments.
"However, should inflation turn out higher and more volatile than expected, a 25-bps rate hike cannot be ruled out," the firm said.
