Title: Nurul Izzah urges continuous reform within PKR and government
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar has called for reform to be pursued continuously within the party as well as in government administration and policies.
She said the party's struggle, born from the reform movement, must not end upon entering government but continue as a legacy for future generations.
"That is why we cannot stop fighting just because we are in government; instead, party members must continue to carry out reform continuously," she said.
She said this when delivering her winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre today.
As an example, Nurul Izzah cited the abolishment of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971, which PKR had long championed and has now realised through government power.
She said the strong economic growth under the Madani Government must also be translated into tangible benefits for the people.
Nurul Izzah said this included increased job opportunities, greater scope for small and medium enterprises, and expanded opportunities for women and youth to participate in the mainstream economy.
"Therefore, structural reforms need to continue to ensure that the salary structure is fairer and wage rates increase in line with productivity," she said.
Meanwhile, she reminded PKR leaders not to view power as personal property, but rather as a trust that must be preserved.
"Positions change, titles fade, names will be silent rather than mentioned, but what remains is the work we leave behind and the values we uphold, and that is what will live on after us," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 25 undocumented migrants fined up to RM10,000 for immigration offences
Article:
PASIR MAS: Twenty-five undocumented migrants were fined between RM5,000 and RM10,000 each by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to various immigration offences.
Judge Zulkpli Abdullah also ordered them to serve between one and three months in jail if they failed to pay the fines.
The group, comprising 16 Bangladeshi men, four Indonesian men, three Indonesian women and two Cambodian men, were among 26 foreigners brought before the court to face charges.
Twelve of the Bangladeshi men were charged under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for overstaying, while the remaining four were charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the same Act for entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit.
The two Cambodian men, four Indonesian men and three Indonesian women were also charged with overstaying.
The foreigners, aged between 21 and 51, were unrepresented during the proceedings, with some assisted by interpreters.
Meanwhile, a 25-year-old Syrian man pleaded not guilty to an overstaying charge.
Zulkpli fixed his case for mention on Sept 13 for the submission of relevant documents.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Khaidijah Khairuddin prosecuted.
The foreigners were arrested in separate operations by the state Immigration Department in Kota Baru and Pasir Puteh between Aug 3 and 6.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three arrested after woman allegedly punched over illegal parking fees in OUG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested three men after a 38-year-old woman was allegedly punched in the head and threatened when she confronted them over illegal parking fee collection in OUG.
A video of the incident went viral yesterday.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the woman lodged a report at 2.38pm yesterday over parking fees being collected at a vacant plot next to the OUG Community Hall in Jalan Awan Besar without the land authority's permission.
He said one of the suspects hurled abuse at the woman before punching her in the head and allegedly threatening to assault her and cause trouble at her workplace.
Police later arrested three men, aged between 20 and 26.
Fadil said checks found all three had previous criminal records.
"The case is being investigated under Sections 506 and 323 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation and voluntarily causing hurt respectively.
"The first suspect was remanded for three days from today until Aug 18, while the other two suspects were each remanded for one day," he said in a statement.
He urged those with information on criminal activities to contact the Brickfields police hotline at 03-2297 9222, Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999 or the nearest police station.
It was reported that an alleged
illegal parking collector
operating along Jalan Hujan in Taman OUG was arrested after repeatedly ignoring enforcement notices and allegedly assaulting an officer during a confrontation.
Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok said the man continued collecting parking fees despite enforcement action by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and other authorities.
She said DBKL and the Federal Territories Director of Lands and Mines Office conducted a site visit the same day and took enforcement action, but the man continued operating.
According to a video shared by Kok, DBKL had issued the man a notice on Aug 4 to cease operations, but he allegedly ignored it.
The video also showed the man confronting enforcement personnel and allegedly assaulting an officer.
Police later arrived and arrested him.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police arrest two suspects in Salak South temple assault case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested two men over an alleged assault that left a man unconscious with severe injuries near a temple in Salak South in April.
Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspects, in their early 30s, were detained around Razak City Residences yesterday.
"The incident was reported on April 9, when a local man in his late 20s was found unconscious near a temple in Salak South.
"The victim had sustained serious injuries, and investigations found that the incident was believed to have stemmed from an argument between the two parties," he said in a statement.
Rosdi said police checks found that the first suspect had a wanted record under Section 354 of the Penal Code for outraging of modesty, while the second had two previous drug-related offences.
Police also seized an iron bracelet believed to have been used in the assault.
Both suspects have been remanded for a day to assist investigations under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
It carries a maximum 20-year jail term, a fine, or whipping upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget to focus on Sabah's blue economy
Article:
TAWAU: Sabah's marine and aquaculture sectors will receive special focus in the preparation of 2027 Budget as the government identifies the Blue Economy as a new strategic area to drive economic growth.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the Federal government is working closely with the Sabah state government to ensure the sector is developed effectively for the benefit of the people.
He said Sabah has strong potential to lead in marine and aquaculture industries, prompting the government to engage with industry players during the 2027 Budget engagement session here today.
"An outcome-based allocation approach will ensure infrastructure investments and financing can accelerate the growth of the marine industry.
"Sabah's natural advantages in marine and aquaculture sectors can be translated into higher-value economic activities through increased productivity, downstream processing, stronger supply chains and better market access," he told a press conference after the session.
Amir Hamzah said the development of the Blue Economy also includes downstream processing activities that can add value to local marine resources.
He cited Sabah's seaweed processing industry, which has successfully penetrated major export markets such as China and the United Kingdom.
"Strengthening the supply chain and downstream processing is expected to create more quality job opportunities and increase the income of local communities," he said.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the government is working closely with the Sabah state government to align proposals under the Sabah Maju Jaya plan with the preparations for 2027 Budget and the 13th Malaysia Plan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 20 undocumented migrants detained in separate Kelantan maritime operations
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: The cover of darkness may have helped migrant smugglers evade a maritime patrol boat, but their movements along Sungai Kelantan eventually led enforcement officers to 20 foreigners believed to have entered the country illegally.
The Kelantan Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) intercepted two groups of undocumented migrants in separate operations this week involving foreigners from India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and Myanmar.
Kelantan Maritime director Kepten Maritim Kamal Mohamad said both operations began after the agency received intelligence about attempts to use unauthorised routes along the river to bring migrants into the country.
He said the first group of four men was detained on Aug 12 after a speedboat was spotted behaving suspiciously in waters off Kuala Besar during an early morning patrol.
"Although the boat managed to escape by speeding into a narrow and shallow river channel, our team immediately deployed to search the riverbank.
"The search led to the arrest of four foreign men aged between 35 and 48," he said here today.
He added that the group comprised three Indians and one Sri Lankan.
Kamal said three of them had passports but could not produce valid travel records proving their legal entry into Malaysia, while the fourth had no travel documents.
Two days later, he said, a similar incident unfolded when another speedboat was detected in the same area in the early hours of Aug 14.
He said the boat again managed to escape into a narrow and shallow stretch of the river, prompting the agency's ground team to continue the search along the riverbank near Tendong, Pasir Mas.
"This time, officers found 16 foreigners, comprising eight Indonesians and the remaining from Myanmar.
"The group comprised five Indonesian men and three women, as well as five Myanmar men and three women, aged between 23 and 50.
"Ten of them had passports but failed to produce valid travel records proving their legal entry into Malaysia, while the remaining six had no identification documents," he said.
Kamal said the 20 people were believed to have entered Malaysia through unauthorised routes and were taken to the agency's headquarters in Kelantan for documentation and investigation.
He said the cases were being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Kamal said the agency would continue to strengthen patrols and enforcement operations in Kelantan waters, particularly in areas believed to be used by syndicates to facilitate cross-border crimes and migrant smuggling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: All 14 delegates debate in favour of DAP remaining in Cabinet ahead of secret ballot
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: All 14 delegates who took the floor to debate the motion on DAP's future in the unity government spoke in favour of remaining in the Cabinet, urging fellow delegates to vote for continued cooperation in the administration.
The debate took place at the DAP national congress at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre, where more than 4,000 delegates are set to vote by secret ballot on whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the government until the end of the parliamentary term.
Kedah delegate Lim Hooi Yee said DAP should not punish the unity government over what she described as a marginal electoral defeat in recent state elections.
She warned that leaving the cabinet would cost the party something far more valuable than a temporary platform to criticise from the outside.
"Don't let this defeat cause us to punish the entire federal government and mortgage the future of the people and the nation.
"If we leave today, will everything be better tomorrow? No — if we leave the government, we may get the space to shout and criticise. But we will lose the most important space of all — a seat at the decision-making table to defend the people's welfare and correct flawed policies," she said during the debate.
She highlighted that choosing to remain in government did not mean DAP would become a yes-man party that stayed silent in the face of policy failures.
"If a policy goes astray, we speak up. On matters of integrity, we are consistent — whether it involves friends or foes. Do not let our party become merely the government's spokesperson to the people.
"Our greater duty is to be the people's spokesperson within the government. Furthermore, our political enemies are eagerly stoking racial and religious sentiments to see us fail. If we leave today, we are handing them a free victory," she said.
Penang delegate Daniel Gooi Zi Sen said it was not DAP that should be leaving, but what he described as enemies from within the unity government itself.
"DAP is a party with a resilient fighting spirit. We all know that our party, particularly in Penang, once reached the heights of success to the point of forming the state government.
"And let us never forget the dark moments we faced in Penang, when even our veteran leaders lost their seats there. If at that time we had despaired and refused to carry on, there would be no way we would today have the achievements we have in Penang, to the point of strengthening the state government.
"We will certainly carry this spirit forward for the party because we are a party that never retreats. We will fight and keep fighting," he said.
Earlier today, secretary-general Anthony Loke
tabled a motion
at the congress for delegates to decide via secret ballot whether to remain in the Cabinet.
The motion, to be decided by more than 4,000 delegates, was seconded by deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming.
Loke, who is also Transport Minister, said the central executive committee (CEC) deliberately refrained from making the call itself — a move aimed at democratising the party's decision-making process.
Last month, the party won only six of the 17 seats it contested in the Johor election.
The party suffered another major setback in the Negri Sembilan election after losing two seats, including Chennah, which had been held by Loke since 2013.
In the Aug 1 state election, Loke failed to retain the seat after losing a straight fight to BN's Siow Kong Choon, the Negri Sembilan MCA Youth chief.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: PKR to remain aligned with BN-Umno while staying loyal to PH partners
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR will continue working with Barisan Nasional and Umno at the federal level while remaining committed to Pakatan Harapan partners DAP and Amanah, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
The PKR president said the decision to maintain cooperation with BN-Umno was made to preserve political stability for the economy, while stressing that PKR would remain loyal to its partners in PH.
"Our choice must be reasonable and wise. There must be loyalty. So I say, we must remain together," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here.
Anwar, who is also the prime minister, said PKR would not compromise on matters involving Islam and its principles, but stressed that Chinese and Indian Malaysians were equally part of the country.
"The Chinese and Indians are also part of our people and fellow citizens. So we will continue this cooperation and always exercise wisdom so that whatever steps are taken do not go overboard," he said.
Turning to PKR's relationship with BN and Umno, Anwar said his preference was to maintain the partnership at the federal level in the interests of political stability and economic prosperity.
"I choose stability. I choose the prosperity of the people through economic strength, and I choose to continue cooperating with Barisan Nasional-Umno at the federal level so that these two principles can continue," he said.
Anwar, however, said this represented his and PKR's position, while other parties would have to decide for themselves how they wished to proceed.
He said PKR was prepared for any eventuality, but maintained that political decisions should be approached rationally and with wisdom.
"As a party of struggle, whatever happens, we are prepared. If we have to fight, we have to fight. But as I said earlier, rationally and with wisdom, we must preserve this unity," he said.
Anwar said his personal relationship with Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi remained good, and expressed confidence that differences between the parties could be resolved through discussions.
He nevertheless said several decisions made by PKR's partners in recent months had caught the party by surprise.
Anwar said while every party had the right to pursue strategies aimed at strengthening itself, cooperation within a coalition required proper consultation among its partners.
He also said PKR will continue cooperation with Gabungan Parti Sarawak and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah, saying the priority among government partners remained maintaining stability until the end of the term, fulfilling their responsibilities and strengthening the country's economy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah publication at PKR National Congress
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched Temu Fikrah, a book published by PKR Youth at the 2026 PKR National Congress.
The 113-page publication, authored by Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement's new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges.
In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation's administration.
He stressed that the initiative was neither mere technocratic rhetoric nor a seasonal political slogan, but a form of civilisational renewal aimed at re-humanising national development.
"Madani strikes a balance between physical progress and spiritual purity, while anchoring the principles of justice, compassion, sustainability and respect in the country's governance," he said.
Anwar also told youth members that the power entrusted to them today represents a heavy responsibility and a test of piety and moral integrity, rather than an opportunity for complacency or celebration of superficial achievements.
He said rebuilding a nation scarred by past injustices and leakages required extraordinary creativity, intellectual courage and spiritual resilience from the young generation.
Meanwhile, Anwar welcomed Temu Fikrah as a manifestation of intellectual enlightenment, expressing hope that it would not merely be read, but internalised and translated into tangible service to the people at the grassroots level.
He said the publication serves as a cadre-building resource, encouraging members to appreciate the history of the struggle, understand the party's foundations and ideals, and internalise the meaning of Reformasi.
Beginning with the emergence of the Reformasi movement and the formation of PKR, the publication explores the principles of justice, policy frameworks, youth activism, and the values of compassion and humanity.
It is also intended to serve as a guide in shaping knowledgeable and principled members who remain steadfast in upholding the mandate of the party's struggle.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: Needs-based aid will benefit Malays most
Article:
AYER KEROH: Malays will remain the biggest beneficiaries of government aid even if it is distributed based on need rather than race, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
He said poverty affected all ethnic groups and aid should therefore be channelled based on need, not race.
"Poverty does not recognise who you are. There are poor Malays, poor Chinese, poor Indians, Ibans and Kadazans. They are all poor," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here.
Saifuddin said Malays would still benefit most because they form the largest segment of the population and therefore account for a significant proportion of those needing assistance.
"When we talk about helping the poor, the biggest beneficiary will be the Malays because they are the largest group. Their percentage is larger.
"So, assistance based on need will automatically protect the majority," he said.
Saifuddin said the approach was not new to PKR, pointing to the Malaysian Economic Agenda championed by party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when the party was in opposition.
He said the party had challenged elements of the New Economic Policy, questioning whether benefits intended for Malays reached ordinary members of the community or mainly benefited elites close to those in power.
Saifuddin said PKR had faced internal resistance over the position but maintained its push for needs-based assistance, which should now be translated into policy as the party is in government.
He said the approach would also move political discourse away from identity politics, arguing that improving people's economic circumstances did not require taking rights away from other communities.
Separately, Saifuddin said he would carry out the deputy president's responsibilities for the remaining period after the party leadership decided deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar would go on leave.
He said he would fulfil the role to the best of his ability alongside the rest of the leadership team.
"The decision was made within the party's forum, namely the Central Leadership Council, and it was announced today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Targeted diesel subsidy system improvements expected in 1-2 months - Amir Hamzah
Article:
TAWAU: Several improvements to the implementation of the targeted diesel subsidy system are being studied, with the government expected to announce them within the next one to two months, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the measures include simplifying the application process, relaxing the eligibility criteria for "sambung bayar" (taking over hire-purchase payments) vehicles, and allowing quotas to be transferred to immediate family members.
"We are still studying several proposals for improvement and, in the next one to two months, we will make an announcement on the improvements, particularly in terms of the process and eligibility," he said at a press conference after attending the Budget 2027 Engagement Session with industry players here today.
Amir Hamzah said preparations for the Budget 2027 would ensure more effective and comprehensive delivery of assistance to the people under the targeted diesel subsidy.
He said the approach was in line with the government's intention to ensure that every allocation provided had a tangible impact and helped ease the cost-of-living burden at the grassroots level.
"Through the Budget 2027 Tour series, we are examining various improvements to the targeted diesel subsidy mechanism to ensure that those who are truly eligible can benefit from it optimally ," he said.
On the implementation of the targeted subsidy in Sabah, Amir Hamzah said about 120,000 owners of pickup trucks and jeeps in the state had been identified as eligible to apply for a diesel subsidy quota of more than 300 litres.
However, he said only about 49,000 eligible vehicle owners had registered and submitted their applications so far.
"The government encourages more eligible owners in Sabah to apply immediately, as the facilities and application channels have already been made available," he said.
To assist those less familiar with technology, Amir Hamzah said the Ministry of Finance had collaborated with the Inland Revenue Board, Urban Transformation Centres and oil companies to provide guidance on applications at counters and petrol stations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar's 79th birthday celebrated as PKR National Congress concludes in Ayer Keroh
Article:
AYER KEROH: The 2026 PKR National Congress concluded today with a celebration of party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's 79th birthday, attended by over 2,000 delegates and observers.
Anwar, who is also prime minister, joined party leaders and delegates in a cake-cutting ceremony during the event.
The occasion also paid tribute to PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, who will be taking a leave of absence from her post, honouring her contributions as a steadfast champion of the reform movement since 1998.
Known as the Srikandi Reformasi, Nurul Izzah was recognised for her long-standing commitment to the party and its reform agenda from a young age, including through periods of political adversity before the formation of the federal government.
Also honoured was Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, one of the key leaders who has remained faithful to the reform cause and PKR since its inception.
The tribute reflected the long journey of PKR's leadership and its foundation built on reform, justice and democracy.
PKR was established in 1999 following the reform movement triggered by Anwar's dismissal as deputy prime minister in 1998, with Parti Keadilan Nasional serving as the primary political vehicle.
The party later merged with Parti Rakyat Malaysia in 2003 to form PKR, strengthening its position as a multiracial political party.
Its founding introduced a political vision centred on social justice, democracy, human rights, transparency and accountable governance.
After more than two decades of political struggle, PKR, alongside its partners in Pakatan Harapan, successfully formed the federal government after winning the 14th General Election in 2018.
Anwar was subsequently sworn in as the 10th prime minister on Nov 24, 2022, following the 15th General Election, leading a coalition government.
Today's birthday celebration symbolised the party's long transition from a grassroots reform movement to a core component of the national administration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: University leaders welcome Auku abolishment, call for balance between freedom, accountability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's plan to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) has been welcomed by public university leaders as a transformative step towards strengthening institutional autonomy, governance and academic freedom.
They said the move demonstrated the government's commitment to comprehensive reform of the higher education ecosystem, while stressing that any new legal framework must strike a clear balance between freedom and accountability.
Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) vice-chancellor Professor Dr Yatimah Alias said the abolishment should be viewed in a broader context, as the legislation governs university establishment, administration and overall governance alongside student affairs.
"The development of a new framework through an inclusive process that takes into account the views of various stakeholders is a welcome step," she said in a statement today.
She added that greater freedom must be accompanied by responsibility, with freedom of expression grounded in facts and respect, while financial autonomy and student activities remain underpinned by transparency.
[[nid:1512312]]
Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the move would give students greater scope to develop mature thinking, strengthen leadership potential and participate constructively in society.
"For IIUM, greater freedom must go hand in hand with responsibility, intellectual integrity and concern for the common good. Students should be given space to critically assess and debate current issues based on knowledge and wisdom," he said.
He said this aspiration aligns with IIUM's commitment to Tawhidic Epistemology and the concept of Ummatic Excellence to produce graduates of strong character and intellectual capability.
Echoing this, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International) and acting vice-chancellor Prof Dr Suriyani Muhamad described the repeal as a "golden opportunity" to clarify public university accountability.
"The new framework must establish a clear balance between autonomy and accountability, freedom and responsibility, as well as innovation and good governance," she said.
She noted that legal reform aligns with the Malaysia Higher Education Plan (2026–2035), which emphasises transformation, excellence and resilience in higher education.
"Reforming university legislation is part of a broader effort to ensure higher education institutions remain relevant, competitive and responsive to future changes and demands," she said.
Meanwhile, Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) voiced support for the Higher Education Ministry's efforts to develop a comprehensive legal framework under the "One Higher Education Act" agenda.
UTeM expressed readiness to work closely with the ministry in stakeholder engagements, stressing the need for a thorough review of the higher education ecosystem.
"This is important to ensure higher education institutions continue to serve as centres of knowledge and civilisation, while playing a role in producing a generation capable of contributing to national and societal development at the international level," it said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in his presidential policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress yesterday, announced that the government would abolish Auku to provide student movements greater freedom and democratic space.s
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP veteran leader urges party to speak up on government issues
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP Women's legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo has urged the party to remain in the Unity Government, but warned that it has stayed silent for too long on scandals within the administration.
"Do we stay or do we go? We stay for now, but the reasons are different than what you have heard today," she said during the debate session at DAP's congress.
She said that while DAP's ministers had a strong record of reform, the party could not ignore deeper problems.
"We cannot run away from the fact that today under our government, Malaysia is more divided on racial lines than ever before," she said.
She said corruption scandals had escalated despite DAP's pledge to eradicate graft.
She cited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's discharge on all 47 corruption charges and the "Corporate Mafia" scandal as issues the party struggled to defend publicly.
"It cannot be defended. Where is DAP? Where is your voice? Why are you silent?" she asked.
She also questioned DAP's ties with Umno and called for a reassessment of its relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"My question is this: I ask our Central Executive Committee to seriously reassess our relationship with Anwar Ibrahim," she said. "What has he done? He has divided us. Pit us against each other, empowered Umno."
She said the decision to stay should not rest solely on promises to deliver reform.
"If we were, we would have done it already," she said, adding that DAP instead needed to use its remaining time in government to rebuild credibility and speak up while still in power.
"Stay in government, find our voices, speak up while we are there.
"And if we must become opposition again, at least we have laid the basis and regained credibility," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP votes on staying in unity government [WATCH]
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Thousands of DAP delegates began casting secret ballots about 1pm today on whether the party should remain in the Federal Government for the rest of the current parliamentary term.
The voting took place at more than 20 stations at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre, with each delegate being given a ballot paper. The process was smooth.
DAP had earlier ruled out a voice vote or a show of hands.
The outcome will determine whether DAP ministers and deputy ministers will remain in the cabinet until the end of the current term, following the party's recent string of state election setbacks.
DAP lost all eight seats it contested in the Sabah
election
last November before suffering further losses in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections. Secretary-general Anthony Loke lost in his Chennah stronghold.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fuziah: PH reform agenda still incomplete after nearly four years
Article:
MELAKA: The reform agenda has yet to be fully realised despite Pakatan Harapan leading the government for nearly four years because few Cabinet members truly understand it, PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Saleh said today.
Fuziah acknowledged that voices remained loud in pointing out that many institutional changes promised by PH had yet to be implemented.
"If people ask why it is difficult to implement institutional reforms in our government today, it is because not many leaders in the Cabinet champion and understand this agenda.
"That is why it is so difficult to bring about institutional reform as we have advocated. Indeed, our president and prime minister is constantly reminded that he is 'not doing enough'.
"But how many share this idea? We ask ourselves, the delegates here, and the leadership at the branch level," she said.
She said this during her winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre today.
Also present was PKR president and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Fuziah said this was among the challenges faced by leadership, but stressed that the party could not remain silent and must instead be more aggressive in explaining the matter to the public.
"We must explain. We must workshop it. We must lecture on it. We must focus. We cannot just keep shouting progressive ideas to those who are not in this frame of mind.
"The task ahead is heavy. We know we want to win, but winning is not easy. It demands discipline and commitment from us in translating thoughts into action," she said.
Following the congress, Fuziah said PKR would organise a workshop to review the achievements of PH and PKR over the past four years and set a new direction.
"We can implement reforms as demanded in the true sense of reform. The Central Leadership Council has committed to holding a workshop in the near future before Merdeka.
"The president has also given his commitment for us to break down and shape a new direction," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-cop fined RM4,500 for threatening to kill wife
Article:
TUMPAT: A former policeman was fined RM4,500 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to threatening to kill his wife last week.
The accused, Muhd Sirrul Akmal Rasali, 43, entered the plea after the charge was read before magistrate Wan Ashrul Afham Mohamad Azmi.
According to the charge, the accused was alleged to have committed criminal intimidation against his 42-year-old wife by threatening to kill her, causing her to feel fearful, at Kampung Semat Jal, Wakaf Bharu, near here at 9am on Aug 8.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of up to seven years or a fine or both upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the accused ran amok in the kitchen of his home in Kampung Semat Jal, Wakaf Bharu at 9am on Aug 8 and acted aggressively towards his wife.
During the incident, the accused uttered words of threat against the complainant, saying he wanted to kill her, which was witnessed by the complainant's mother and child.
Fearing for her safety, the complainant contacted the Tumpat district police headquarters control room, leading to the arrest of the accused.
Investigations revealed the cause of the incident was the accused's dissatisfaction with his mother-in-law, who frequently interfered in their marriage.
Prosecuting officer Inspector Megat Asyraf Megat Ishak appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Afiqah Amran.
Earlier, Megat Asyraf requested an appropriate sentence for the accused.
However, Afiqah appealed for a minimum sentence, stating that Sirrul Akmal regretted his actions, worked as a village labourer earning RM50 a day, and supported two schooling children.
She added that the accused suffers from mental health issues and is undergoing psychiatric treatment at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital in Kota Baru.
The court subsequently imposed a fine of RM4,500, or nine months' imprisonment in default.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea's Kim tells Putin he is 'proud' of strong ties
Article:
SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un told Russian President Vladimir Putin he was "proud" of their countries' strong ties, state media reported Sunday, after providing military support for Moscow's war against Ukraine.
Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say.
"I am always proud to be able to expect more excellent future of the bilateral relations by leading, together with you, the DPRK-Russia ties that has carried forward the history of common struggle," Kim said in his letter to Putin, according to an English-language dispatch by the official Korean Central News Agency.
DPRK is the acronym for the North's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
Kim added that he had a "firm belief" that Russia would thrive and defend its "territorial integrity" under Putin's "wise leadership."
In a letter to Kim delivered on Friday to mark Korea's liberation from Japanese colonial rule at the end of World War II, Putin said relations between the two countries had reached the "unprecedentedly high level of comprehensive strategic partnership."
"Our states are actively cooperating in all the sectors while making concerted efforts to ensure the regional security and stability," the Russian leader said.
The exchange of letters follows Ukraine's accusation this month that Moscow had launched North Korean ballistic missiles in a strike that killed at least nine people and wounded dozens.
Kyiv has also recently said that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are due to deploy to Russia, although it has provided no evidence to back the claim or a timeframe for the deployment.
In making the claim, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy asked Seoul to supply air defence systems to protect against Russian missiles, a request that has gone unanswered by the South.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar seeks stronger governance rules for state-owned entities
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will soon bring a proposed law on state-owned enterprises to the Cabinet to ensure all government-owned entities are subject to clear and consistent governance rules.
Delivering his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress here today, Anwar said the proposed legislation would establish common standards for state-owned entities, including agencies that had previously operated with a degree of autonomy.
He said such entities could not regard themselves as being exempt from established rules simply because of their status as government agencies or state-owned bodies.
"I will bring to the Cabinet soon a State-Owned Enterprise (Bill), a law governing government-owned entities, so that everyone must comply.
"They cannot think that just because they are an agency, they are free to do as they please. They must follow the rules and regulations.
"This is what we call good governance," the PKR president said.
Anwar said weaknesses in the management and investment activities of government-linked entities had surfaced in the past, citing investigations into Majlis Amanah Rakyat's (Mara) purchase of properties in Australia as an example.
He said such cases underscored the need for stronger and more consistent oversight of government-owned entities.
Anwar said the government's push to strengthen governance would also extend beyond issues involving Tabung Haji and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda).
He said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, called him today and referred to his remarks on investigations into governance issues involving Tabung Haji and Felda.
Anwar said the King reiterated that scrutiny should be extended to other agencies facing similar problems.
"He said, 'Continue with all the agencies that have problems'," Anwar said.
He added that the government would address such weaknesses through investigations, stronger rules and corrective action, rather than merely making allegations.
Anwar said the same approach would be taken in reviewing issues involving Tabung Haji, with the government studying arguments raised in Parliament and considering amendments to the Tabung Haji Act to meet present-day governance requirements.
"That is how we deal with these problems — not by merely complaining, but by taking action," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM Anwar vows full repeal of AUKU, no replacement laws curbing student freedom or movement
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — The government has given an assurance that the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will be fully repealed without introducing any new laws that restrict or suppress student movements.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim stressed that he himself would raise the matter at the Cabinet meeting.
“There are concerns that sometimes AUKU is repealed and a new law is introduced that also restricts them.
“I also do not agree with any amendment or replacement (law) that restricts or suppresses student activities,” said Anwar, who is also PKR president.
He said this when delivering his winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Elaborating, Anwar said existing legal provisions, including those relating to criminal offences, are sufficient to address any misconduct that may be committed by student groups.
He said that as citizens, students are subject to the general laws applicable to everyone if they commit an offence.
“Students are ordinary citizens. There are criminal laws and there are laws that apply to everyone.
“If they assault someone, if they cause injury, or if they cheat in an examination, the existing laws are sufficient (for punishment),” he said.
AUKU has previously undergone seven rounds of amendments since it was introduced in 1971, including amendments in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments in 2024 to Section 16B saw disciplinary action against students at public universities no longer fall under the authority of the vice-chancellor, but instead be decided by the Student Disciplinary Committee.
In addition, amendments to Section 15A allow student representative councils and student bodies to raise funds and receive contributions in any manner, subject to the regulations and written laws currently in force. — Bernama

Title: Dungun doctor duped in forex, Ethereum scam, loses RM558,000 through 77 transactions
Article:
DUNGUN, Aug 16 — A female doctor at a private clinic here lost RM558,000 after falling victim to an online forex and Ethereum coin investment scam since January.
Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 32-year-old victim initially saw an advertisement offering trading and investment lessons before contacting an individual via Instagram.
She was later contacted by an individual known as “Wan” on WhatsApp and made 77 transactions to six accounts between January 12 and August 11, losing RM558,000.
“The victim was later told she had committed an offence and needed to pay compensation to avoid legal action, but realised she had been cheated after receiving no returns,” he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, in Kuala Terengganu, a retired civil servant lost RM92,781 after being duped by a fake online loan scheme.
District police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 60-year-old victim responded to a Facebook advertisement in June offering loans with low interest rates and attractive terms.
The victim, who applied for a RM10,000 personal loan, was instructed to make payments for purported processing fees and eventually transferred RM92,781 through 86 transactions to 28 accounts between June 14 and August 13.
“He was also forced to provide personal details and continued to receive threats of legal action before lodging a police report,” he said in a statement.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Nurul Izzah: I remain committed to same reform spirit since 1998
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar remains committed to the same spirit of struggle that drove the reform movement when it began in 1998,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
According to the report, Nurul Izzah said although she would carry out her responsibilities through a different avenue in the future, her goals remained the same — strengthening institutions, preserving dignity and creating more opportunities for Malaysians.
“PKR will continue to carry this responsibility. I too will continue to carry this responsibility through a different avenue, but I will move forward with the same purpose.
“To strengthen institutions, preserve dignity, open up opportunities for more Malaysians and help build a fairer Malaysia,” she was quoted as saying in her winding-up speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade and Convention Centre (MITC) in Melaka yesterday.
She said the shared history of the struggle with PKR members had been among the most important things that shaped her since 1998.
According to the report, she said she would continue to uphold the principle of standing with those who remained loyal during the most difficult times.
“At that time, I was not even 19 when Keadilan was formed, and because of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), I could not even become a member.
“This is about our shared history. In every ceramah we held, even when the sense of loneliness was overwhelming.
“The most important thing I learnt was that we need to stand with those who stood with us during the most difficult times. Brothers and sisters, you are all my family. I grew up with all of you.
“May Allah SWT protect PKR. I am Nurul Izzah Anwar, the same Nurul Izzah Anwar as in 1998!” she was quoted as saying.
Nurul Izzah also said the reform struggle would take time and involve various parties within the democratic system, including voters and other centres of power.
She also touched on her involvement in writing, saying she was now no longer allowed to write a political column.
“In the past, we did not have control or shareholdings in the media, and today we still do not have control or majority shareholdings in the media.
“I was also instructed that I could not write a column about politics. I was also warned about this,” she reportedly said.

Title: Diesel subsidy shake‑up coming soon; govt promises simpler rules, family quota transfers, easier access
Article:
TAWAU, Aug 16 — Several improvements to the implementation of the targeted diesel subsidy system are being studied, with the government expected to announce them within the next one to two months, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the measures include simplifying the application process, relaxing the eligibility criteria for
sambung bayar
(taking over hire-purchase payments) vehicles, and allowing quotas to be transferred to immediate family members.
“We are still studying several proposals for improvement and, in the next one to two months, we will make an announcement on the improvements, particularly in terms of the process and eligibility,” he said at a press conference after attending the 2027 Budget Engagement Session with industry players here today.
Amir Hamzah said preparations for the 2027 Budget would ensure more effective and comprehensive delivery of assistance to the people under the targeted diesel subsidy.
He said the approach was in line with the government’s intention to ensure that every allocation provided had a tangible impact and helped ease the cost-of-living burden at the grassroots level.
“Through the 2027 Budget Tour series, we are examining various improvements to the targeted diesel subsidy mechanism to ensure that those who are truly eligible can benefit from it optimally,” he said.
On the implementation of the targeted subsidy in Sabah, Amir Hamzah said about 120,000 owners of pickup trucks and jeeps in the state had been identified as eligible to apply for a diesel subsidy quota of more than 300 litres.
However, he said only about 49,000 eligible vehicle owners had registered and submitted their applications so far.
“The government encourages more eligible owners in Sabah to apply immediately, as the facilities and application channels have already been made available,” he said.
To assist those less familiar with technology, Amir Hamzah said the Ministry of Finance had collaborated with the Inland Revenue Board, Urban Transformation Centres and oil companies to provide guidance on applications at counters and petrol stations. — Berrnama

Title: PKR leaders vow fairness for all races, slam racial propaganda, urge unity over ego
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR must continue to defend a fair political approach to all sections of society, while respecting the position of Islam and the Malays in the Federal Constitution.
PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the position of Islam and the Malays is a core element in the Federal Constitution that must be respected by all parties.
“But at the same time, we are fair to all Malays, Chinese, Indians, Christians, Buddhists and Hindus,” he said when delivering his closing speech on the second day of the PKR National Congress at Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
The Selangor Menteri Besar said the reform struggle initiated by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 1998 had succeeded in mainstreaming various issues including the enrichment of democracy and fundamental rights, fair economic distribution and government administration with integrity.
In line with Amirudin, PKR vice president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan wanted PKR to remain firm in defending the diversity of races in this country and strongly reject actions that use racial issues as political capital.
Ramanan, who is also the Minister of Human Resources, said the stance was important to ensure that the harmony of the people remained guaranteed and was not undermined by narrow political agendas.
“In our country’s politics, there are parties who deliberately play on racial issues to gain votes and divide unity for their own interests. However, PKR must continue to be a party that firmly defends diversity and strongly rejects such actions,” he said.
Ramanan also called on the entire leadership and party members to prioritise unity and put aside personal egos in order to strengthen the party machinery at all levels.
“If we fight among ourselves at the top, the ones who end up being the victims are the machinery below. The branches are affected, the branches are affected, the members are confused, the machinery becomes weak and ultimately our political opponents benefit. We must work together as one family,” he said.
Another vice president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said the party’s durability and effectiveness did not depend on propaganda on racial issues, but rather was proven through the increasing support of people of various races for elected representatives who served with distinction.
He said this could be seen through the results of the Chennah seat in the Negeri Sembilan State Election which saw Malay voters’ support for DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke show a positive increase, despite facing identity politics propaganda. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says any decision on Umno must prioritise people’s welfare, ‘not anger’
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told party delegates today that he chose to put the people first, amid growing internal censure against the party’s unity government ally Barisan Nasional.
Speaking at this year’s congress, Anwar said any decision regarding PKR’s cooperation with BN and Umno must not be driven by anger, but instead treated carefully through what he described as political “wisdom” that ultimately puts national interests above partisan conflicts.
Still, Anwar suggested the party will not hesitate to langgar — a Malay term for engaging in battle or demolishing a foe — if PKR or Pakatan Harapan is forced to.
“With regards to Umno-BN, whatever the decision it cannot be based on our disappointment or anger,” the PKR president said in his winding-up speech, amid boos and jeers towards Umno from delegates on the floor.
“It must always be driven by public and national interests. You may say they (Umno-BN) care less about the people, I say we must care. Because we should be the rational one, and there must be wisdom and insights.
“The pact of the unity government would not have been possible if not for wisdom, without the realisation and utmost love for the country,” Anwar added.
Anwar succeeded in keeping the uneasy alliance with rivals Umno stable since the two formed the so-called unity government in 2022, but the relationship was said to have soured after the Malay nationalists’ decided to team up with Perikatan Nasional at the Negeri Sembilan state elections.
The alliance is also seen as the source of PKR’s internal friction, which had led to acrimonious departure of several senior politicians.
At the same time, PH’s strongest component member by seat size, the DAP, is also reviewing its position after the party suffered one of its worst electoral performance in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan since 2008.
Today, Anwar reiterated his position to keep the PH-BN alliance alive until the coming general election, again citing stability and “prosperity” as the main motivation. The PH chairman also said his personal relationship with Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi remains “strong”.
“If you ask me this is my choice. But what is their choice let them answer,” he said.
“And we as a party that fights (for the people) we are always ready regardless,” Anwar said.
“If we must langgar then we will langgar but as I said earlier, by being rational and full of wisdom we must protect this unity because at the personal level my ties with Datuk Seri Zahid Hamidi is still very strong.”

Title: Woman punched, threatened in OUG parking row; KL police arrest three suspects with records (VIDEO)
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 16 — Police have arrested three men after a woman reported being assaulted and threatened during an alleged illegal parking fee collection near the OUG community hall in Jalan Awan Besar.
The 38 year old complainant told officers she was verbally abused before being punched in the head and threatened with further violence, including disruption at her workplace.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said three suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were detained following the incident. Checks revealed all had prior criminal records.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation and Section 323 for voluntarily causing hurt.
A remand order was obtained for the first suspect for three days from August 16 to 18, while the other two were remanded for one day each.
Police urged the public to report any information on crime to the Brickfields police hotline at 03 22979222, the Kuala Lumpur hotline at 03 21159999, or the nearest police station.
