Title: Malaysian Qualifications Agency says abolition of AUKU cannot be taken lightly, urges clear guidelines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) must be followed by the creation of an equivalent legal framework to guarantee the continuity of governance and quality of the country’s higher education at the global level.
Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Prof Datuk Dr Mohammad Shatar Sabran said any changes to the higher education legal framework must be made comprehensively and carefully to avoid gaps in terms of regulations, governance and institutional monitoring.
He said the higher education system needs clear guidelines and procedures to ensure that university management and administration remain orderly and accountable.
“Any decision regarding the abolition of AUKU must be preceded by a comprehensive approach as recommended by the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT), including a comprehensive assessment of the implications of changes to the higher education ecosystem.
“This approach is important to ensure that efforts to strengthen the country’s higher education system do not affect the government’s agenda to make Malaysia a global education hub,” he said in a statement today.
Mohammad Shatar said any proposal to abolish AUKU cannot be viewed lightly because the act is one of the important instruments that provides guidelines and a governance framework for the journey of higher education institutions (IPT).
Mohammad Shatar said the quality of national education today is highly regarded by the world and efforts to build the quality of national education that have been implemented since Merdeka need to be further strengthened.
In this regard, he called on the public to give full trust to KPT in its efforts to discuss matters related to the act.
He said it was also in line with the Malaysian Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035 which was launched in January through the agenda of the One Higher Education Act.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, while delivering the PKR Presidential Policy Address in conjunction with the PKR 2026 National Congress yesterday, announced that the government would abolish AUKU to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in the country.
Anwar said the decision was made following a memorandum and the views of the student leadership who wanted comprehensive changes to AUKU. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak skies turn grey, DOE warns haze plumes from Kalimantan push API into danger zone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 11am today, with the Serian district police headquarters (IPD) topping the list at 162.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said two other areas, Samarahan and Kuching, recorded API readings of 155 and 132, respectively, believed to be due to haze smoke moving in from various directions.
She said 65 other areas recorded moderate air quality levels.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah said according to the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report on August 15, 132 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 115 in Sumatra and six in Malaysia, comprising one each in Melaka and Johor and two each in Sarawak and Sabah.
“The Regional Haze Map released by ASMC today shows hotspots scattered across most of Kalimantan, with isolated hotspots also detected on Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, Sulawesi and southern Sumatra,” she said in a statement today.
Azuri Azizah said moderate smoke plumes were observed over southern and western Kalimantan, while light, localised smoke plumes were detected in southern and central Sumatra.
However, she said widespread cloud cover hampered observation of the current hotspot and haze situation.
She said the DOE had stepped up enforcement and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, in addition to regularly monitoring API readings.
“The National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate government agencies’ actions in dealing with open burning and the haze situation,” she said.
The public is urged to refrain from open burning and immediately report any such activities or fire incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution made PKR’s de facto number two as Nurul Izzah steps down
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution will take over the duties of PKR’s deputy president after incumbent Nurul Izzah Anwar announced she would “take leave”.
Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the handover at the party’s congress here this afternoon, where Nurul Izzah also gave a parting speech that called on the party to unite and galvanise its “differences” as a form of strength.
Anwar also gave full authority to PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to direct the party’s election campaigns, a move he suggested would streamline preparations and strategies to avoid confusion in the chain of command.
“He (Saifuddin) has been with me for decades and I know him very well,” Anwar said in a speech as he wound up this year’s congress.
”As for Amirudin he is given full trust… no more various ways. This time it’s one system, one strategy and a unified approach. Everyone must follow,” he added.
Two days ago Nurul Izzah cautioned the party about factionalism, saying that the party cannot remain strong if it is distracted by internal disputes.
Speaking at the joint Wanita Keadilan and Angkatan Muda Keadilan congress, she said the party risked weakening itself if factionalism continued to dominate.
Nurul Izzah, Anwar’s eldest daughter, said she will remain in the party but pursue a different path in her political struggle, expressing a preference for field work with civil society groups.
“You cannot please everyone; you can only remain true to yourself,” she said when opening the 2026 Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) and Wanita PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh on Friday.

Title: At DAP congress, most delegates back staying in Anwar govt, urge faster reforms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates debating whether the party should remain in the federal government today have largely backed staying until the end of the current term, while urging Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to accelerate reforms promised to Malaysians.
Speaking during the party’s national congress here, several delegates argued that leaving the unity government now would amount to abandoning voters and handing political advantage to rival parties.
Perak delegate and Sitiawan assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yeong said his position was simple: DAP should remain in the government until the end of the term.
“Previously, we fought and kept fighting until we won. Now that we have won, do we want to run away? No. We should stay once again,” he said.
Ng acknowledged DAP’s setbacks in the recent state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, but said the defeats should prompt the party to push harder for change rather than leave the government.
“We have to accept that this unity government has weaknesses. We need to accept that changes must be made, and we should urge our leaders and the PM to implement the reforms promised to the people, instead of leaving the government and disappointing the people even more,” he said.
He also questioned who would benefit if DAP walked away.
“If we leave, who benefits? Who will be happy? The answer may be MCA, PAS or Perikatan Nasional, which may take over the federal government after this,” he said.
Penang delegate Daniel Gooi Zi Sen, meanwhile, stressed the importance of political stability, pointing to the disruption caused by the Sheraton Move in 2020.
He said major projects had stalled during the period of political instability, while projects such as the LRT were now moving forward under the current administration.
“We cannot let political turmoil happen again,” he said, before asking delegates: “Did we fail as a federal government? Did we not do our job?”
Gooi’s argument was that the party should not disregard the progress made under the unity government despite its shortcomings.
Sarawak delegate Soo Tien Ren said he too would vote for DAP to remain in government, warning that leaving now would amount to “political suicide”.
“If we leave now, we will be committing political suicide. We will be abandoning Malaysians who believe in us, and abandoning our responsibility to correct our own mistakes,” he said.
However, Soo cautioned that merely remaining in Cabinet without clearly demonstrating what reforms DAP was pursuing could also prove politically damaging.
“If we stay, and all we can say is we remain in Cabinet and push for more reforms, but without telling Malaysians the reforms and the target, then staying turns into immediate political suicide and into slow political death.
“Between immediate suicide and slow death, I choose neither. I choose this party to survive and recover.”
Soo said DAP must acknowledge that it had not performed well enough and push Anwar for further reforms, including for the prime minister to relinquish the Finance portfolio and for the Budi95 subsidised petrol scheme to be restored to a 300-litre quota.
Kedah delegate Lim Hooi Yee similarly called on DAP to remain in the federal government until the end of the term.
“DAP must remain in the federal government until the end of the term. Leaving would mean betraying the King, the people and the principles of the party, which has fought for the people of Malaysia.
“The struggle is not over,” she said.
Lim said the results of the three state elections should instead serve as a warning for DAP to reflect on its performance.
“The results of the three state elections gave us different warnings. They are for us to reflect on, not to wash our hands of the matter and run away from responsibility,” she said.
DAP delegates are currently voting on whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the federal government.
The vote comes after party secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said he would leave the decision on DAP’s continued participation in the government to delegates.
The outcome is expected to be announced this afternoon.

Title: At DAP congress, Sangeet urges rethink of ties with Anwar, says PM has divided coalition, empowered Umno
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Wanita DAP legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo today called on the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) to reassess its relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of a vote at the national congress on whether DAP should remain in the federal government.
While favouring DAP’s continued participation in the federal government, Sangeet said the current coalition arrangement under Anwar had failed to unite its partners.
“Instead of bringing the coalition partners together, what has he done?
“He has divided us, pitted one against the other and empowered Umno.
“We cannot afford to ignore that,” she said in her debate speech on the motion to decide the party’s position in the federal unity government.
Sangeet said DAP’s decision to remain in the federal government should not be based merely on preserving political stability ahead of the next general election, but on using the remaining period to rebuild public trust, regain its voice and address issues on which it had previously remained silent.
“At the ministerial level, initiatives have been strong but we cannot ignore the larger problems that we are facing as a party.
“On too many issues, we have remained silent because we didn’t want to rock the boat,” she said.
She said the party could not ignore growing racial divisions and corruption-related scandals during its time in the federal government, warning that its silence on these issues had affected public confidence.
“We cannot run away from the fact that today, under our government, Malaysia is more divided on racial lines than ever before.
“We cannot deny that there are scandals relating to corruption that have escalated during the time that we have been in power,” she said.
She added that DAP came into power promising to eradicate corruption but questioned whether the party had done enough to address the issue.
“We have faced scandals involving our institutions, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), and our voters are asking: ‘Where is DAP? Where is your voice? Why are you silent?’”
She was referring to allegations of a so-called “corporate mafia” involving claims of collusion with the MACC to manipulate corporate takeovers through extortion and the exploitation of regulatory loopholes, including allegations implicating former MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki.
“I can assure you that when the scandal of the corporate mafia hit our news, our leaders in Cabinet stood there and asked themselves how they were going to defend this? It cannot be defended,” she added.
Sangeet also questioned whether DAP could genuinely work with its coalition partners, particularly Umno, which she said continued to openly attack the party despite being part of the federal government.
“But I do not say that it is because we are going to achieve the reforms we have promised all this while because if we were, we would have done it already.
“The fact is we cannot work with these coalition partners,” she said.
Sangeet said DAP should use the next 18 months in government to speak up on issues of concern and rebuild its credibility.

Title: Gobind says DAP must chase reforms Unity partners can deliver, not manifesto wish‑lists
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP must use the results of recent state elections as a basis to reassess its direction and ensure the party remains relevant in the country’s evolving political landscape, its national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said.
He said this was important after three and a half years of DAP’s participation in the Unity Government, allowing the party to review its achievements and shortcomings during the period before charting its future course.
“We accept the decision of the people, the people’s choice. But the results have prompted us to reconsider how we should move forward,” he said in his welcoming speech at the DAP Party Conference 2026 at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
Also present were party secretary-general Anthony Loke, vice-chairmen Chong Chieng Jen, Teo Nie Ching, Ng Suee Lim, Syahredzan Johan and J. Arul Kumar, as well as DAP advisers Lim Guan Eng and Tan Kok Wai.
Gobind said that as part of a multi-party government, DAP needed to be realistic by prioritising reforms that could secure consensus among the coalition partners, rather than seeking to implement the party’s entire manifesto on its own.
“We need to look at what can actually be agreed upon by all the parties and implemented, so that we can ensure the reforms or changes that need to be made are carried out,” he said.
Gobind also proposed that a special Parliament sitting be convened soon to debate and approve amendments to key laws, including the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA), as part of efforts to advance the institutional reform agenda.
He said the proposed amendments should also cover the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012, the separation of the Attorney General’s and Public Prosecutor’s powers, as well as limiting the Prime Minister’s tenure to two terms.
“These steps are important to show that the government is truly serious about institutional reform, to ensure transparent governance and prevent the abuse of power,” he said.
On the economy, Gobind said the government needed to better understand the challenges faced by the people and take measures to ease their burden, while maintaining political stability to attract foreign investment.
“We want to ensure that we can move forward by understanding the challenges actually faced by society. The government needs to take action to ease the burden on the people, particularly in terms of the economy,” he said.
He said political stability was important in convincing foreign investors to choose Malaysia as an investment destination, which would in turn create more job opportunities.
The conference today is expected to see Loke table a motion on whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the government bloc until the end of the 16th Parliament term.
A total of 4,264 delegates from 1,704 eligible branches will decide on the motion through a secret ballot after the debate.
This year’s conference is also being held in conjunction with the 60th anniversary of DAP’s establishment.
The party is one of the three main component parties of Pakatan Harapan (PH), alongside PKR and Amanah. — Bernama

Title: Aminuddin says he’ll take responsibility, ready to quit PKR Negeri Sembilan role after polls loss
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Former Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has expressed his readiness to step down as chairman of the Negeri Sembilan State Leadership Council (MPN) of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) following the recent state election.
Aminuddin said he agreed with the demands of six PKR branch leaders in the state who are urging the party leadership to reassess its position after PKR only won two of the 15 state assembly seats contested.
“I also take note of the demands of the six Negeri Sembilan branch leaders who want me to take responsibility for the defeat. I would like to state publicly that I agree with your demands.
“I also accept this responsibility I am leading so I am ready to be responsible. I don’t want to run away from responsibility and I don’t want to hide behind various excuses,” he said.
He said this when delivering his closing speech on the second day of the National Congress of the Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) at Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Aminuddin said he left the final decision to the party leadership and was ready to accept any action for the future of PKR.
“The position is not mine, the trust belongs to the party. If the party sees that there is a decision that needs to be made for the future of Keadilan, I agree.
“But I would like to emphasise that defeat will not be a reason to stop fighting, on the contrary, this defeat must be the starting point for rebuilding and this is what we hope for,” he said.
In the Negeri Sembilan state election on August 1, PKR only managed to defend two seats, namely the Chuah and Sri Tanjung seats out of the total 15 constituencies contested in the state.
Apart from that, Aminuddin, who contested in the Linggi state seat, lost by a majority of 2,976 votes in a three-cornered race involving the incumbent from Barisan Nasional (BN) Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Bersatu candidate Datuk Zamri Md Said.
Aminuddin received 6,163 votes while Datuk Mohd Faizal (9,139 votes) and Zamri (391 votes). — Bernama

Title: No MACC arrest, just rumours: Abdul Azeez’s son rebuts social media buzz over Tabung Haji RCI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The son of former Baling Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has dismissed claims that have gone viral on social media that his father was arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) last night.
Mohamed Khairul Azman Abdul Azeez, through a post on Facebook today, said his father is currently at their residence and resting, thus denying unfounded reports regarding his arrest in connection with the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report.
“For those who have been asking about him, I would like to thank him very much and for your information, my father is still at home resting. Hopefully everything will be facilitated and any form of investigation will be carried out with full integrity, fairness and transparency,” he said.
Rumours about the arrest of Abdul Azeez, who is also the former chairman of Tabung Haji, began to spread widely on several social media platforms since late last night.
Abdul Azeez had previously stated that he would cooperate fully if investigated regarding the Tabung Haji RCI Report which was made public on July 29.
Last Tuesday, a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat was held to allow the report to be tabled and debated by Dewan Rakyat members. — Bernama

Title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah, PKR Youth’s manifesto‑meets‑manual for courage, creativity and Madani governance
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched
Temu Fikrah
, a publication produced by the PKR Youth wing (AMK) in conjunction with the PKR National Congress 2026.
The 113-page publication, authored by AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and AMK executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement’s new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges.
In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation’s administration.
He stressed that the initiative was neither mere technocratic rhetoric nor a seasonal political slogan, but a form of civilisational renewal aimed at re-humanising national development.
“Madani strikes a balance between physical progress and spiritual purity, while anchoring the principles of justice, compassion, sustainability and respect in the country’s governance,” he said.
Anwar also reminded youths, particularly AMK members, that the power entrusted to them today represents a heavy responsibility and a test of piety and moral integrity, rather than an opportunity for complacency or celebration of superficial achievements.
He said rebuilding a nation scarred by past injustices and leakages required extraordinary creativity, intellectual courage and spiritual resilience from the young generation.
Meanwhile, Anwar welcomed
Temu Fikrah
as a manifestation of intellectual enlightenment, expressing hope that it would not merely be read, but internalised and translated into tangible service to the people at the grassroots level.
He said the publication serves as an AMK cadre-building resource, encouraging members to appreciate the history of the struggle, understand the party’s foundations and ideals, and internalise the meaning of “Reformasi”.
Beginning with the emergence of the Reformasi movement and the formation of PKR, the publication explores the principles of justice, policy frameworks, youth activism, and the values of compassion and humanity.
It is also intended to serve as a guide in shaping knowledgeable and principled members who remain steadfast in upholding the mandate of the party’s struggle. — Bernama

Title: PKR’s 27‑year struggle isn’t about power, Zaliha says it’s about changing how Malaysia is run
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Becoming a government is not the end of the Reformasi struggle but rather a real test to prove the courage and wisdom to implement change, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa.
She said the reformasi struggle led by PKR for 27 years should not be seen simply as an effort to take over the country’s administration, but rather aimed at changing the way the country is governed.
“Since when has the cry for reform been just a slogan to get into Putrajaya? If our 27-year struggle is only aimed at changing who sits in the government seat, then our struggle is too small.
“Our main goal is to change the way this country is governed,” she said when delivering her winding up speech at the PKR 2026 National Congress at Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), here today.
Zaliha said that after PKR became part of the government, the party now shouldered a great responsibility to translate the reform agenda through strengthening institutions and governance, combating corruption and abuse of power, as well as ensuring that justice could be felt by all levels of the people.
She said that apart from that, PKR members also need to be brave enough to reprimand and correct any weaknesses that arise among themselves.
“Implementing reform also requires wisdom. Reform does not mean that everything must be changed overnight. There are priorities that need to be determined...there are changes that can be made immediately, and there are changes that require time, negotiation and preparation so that they truly last,” she said.
Taking a lesson from the story of Khalifah Umar Abdul Aziz as touched upon by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in his speech at the congress opening yesterday, Zaliha said changes need to be implemented in stages without sacrificing the goals of the struggle.
“Gradually does not mean delaying. Being cautious does not mean we have lost the courage to carry out reforms. What is important is that our direction must be clear. We must know what needs to be corrected and we must continue to move towards it,” she said.
Meanwhile, Zaliha, who is also the Member of Parliament for Sekijang, said PKR needs to streamline party communication so that the government’s achievements can be understood and felt by the people.
She said the government cannot assume that the people will know and understand an achievement just because a policy or programme has been implemented.
“I completely agree. We cannot complain that the people do not understand us if we ourselves fail to explain. “After this congress, I hope we can see a more structured, faster and closer to the language of the people party communication movement,” she said.
She also urged the party to master the narrative on social media and not let the space be dominated by the opposition.
According to Zaliha, victory in terms of numbers and policies does not necessarily guarantee acceptance by the people if the party fails to win their “feelings”, thus not taking lightly the importance of mastering the narrative field. — Bernama

Title: DAP’s destiny on the table as Anthony Loke leaves Unity decision to Putrajaya delegates
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — The DAP Party Conference today is the appropriate forum to decide whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the Unity Government, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
The Transport Minister said such a major decision should be made collectively by the more than 4,000 delegates attending the conference, rather than solely by the 40 members of the Central Executive Committee (CEC).
“We discussed this in the CEC and decided to leave it to the delegates to determine whether the party should remain in the federal government or not. Therefore, the delegates have to make a collective decision for the party.
“As a party in government, there are certainly some constraints and weaknesses that we have to bear together. Therefore, the leadership is leaving it to the delegates to assess whether we should remain in the government until the end of its term or play the role of a pressure group,” he said.
He said this when delivering his policy speech at the 2026 DAP Party Conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.
Also present were DAP advisers Lim Guan Eng and Tan Kok Wai, national chairman Gobind Singh Deo, national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, as well as the party’s entire leadership.
Loke also acknowledged that DAP still faces challenges in securing support from Malay voters, following his defeat in the Chennah seat in the recent 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election.
He said his candidacy in the Malay-majority constituency was not aimed at pursuing a personal victory, but rather at proving that DAP could garner support from voters of various races, including in Malay-majority areas.
“I was unable to retain the Chennah seat. I apologise to the delegates for the defeat. I contested not for a personal victory. I contested despite the difficulties because I wanted to prove that DAP can gain the support of voters of various races and that we can win in Malay-majority areas,” he said.
The DAP conference is being held in Putrajaya for the first time. — Bernama

Title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates for losing Chennah in Negeri Sembilan polls
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today apologised to party delegates for failing to retain Chennah, a seat he had held for three consecutive terms since 2013, in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election.
Loke said contesting the challenging seat was never about personal achievement, but about demonstrating that DAP could win support from people of various ethnic backgrounds and succeed in a Malay-majority area.
“I felt saddened that as the party secretary-general I was unable to retain the seat in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election and for that I would like to apologise to all the delegates for this defeat.
“However, I acknowledge that this mission was unsuccessful and we did not receive strong support from Malay voters or the Orang Asli community.
“This is a major challenge for DAP, how we can break through this racial barrier so that our political journey can go further,” he said in his policy speech during the party’s national congress at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.
In the recent Negeri Sembilan state election, Loke lost to MCA’s John Kong Choon, who won the seat with a majority of 688 votes.
Nevertheless, Loke stressed that the party’s recent string of electoral defeats should not prevent it from moving forward, as every election has its winners and losers.
“We have almost 60 years of electoral experience and we suffered many defeats during our early struggles but we must not give up.
“To the delegates and party activists, let this be our motivation and inspiration and as long as we do not give up, DAP’s future can still be embraced by the majority of Malaysians,” he said.
Today’s congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party’s position and future direction within the Unity Government.
The congress comes amid growing debate over slow reforms and electoral setbacks within the party, including whether it should remain part of the administration under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Title: Asyraf Wajdi suspends MARA staff after eight students allege sexual harassment misconduct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) has immediately suspended a member of its staff following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a MARA educational institution.
MARA chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation to be conducted without interference from the parties involved.
He said the matter came to light after receiving direct messages from several students claiming to be victims, prompting him to order MARA management to take immediate action.
“I tried hard to persuade them to file a police report, as this involves a criminal matter. I find it curious that these students are more willing to complain directly to me than to the management,” he said in a Facebook post.
Asyraf Wajdi said MARA would never compromise on any form of misconduct and gave an assurance that no cases would be covered up or silenced in an effort to protect the institution’s reputation.
“Do not be afraid to report any misconduct, especially regarding sexual harassment. MARA will never compromise on such misconduct and will take stern action, including dismissal, against those involved,” he said. — Bernama

Title: DAP backs Anwar ‘100 per cent’ on AUKU repeal, Loke says reforms must go further
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP today said it will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim “100 per cent” in abolishing the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), but stressed that the same spirit must be extended to other promised reforms.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said education reform should go beyond the abolition of AUKU and focus on ensuring equal access to higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.
“AUKU is one component, but what is more important in education reform is to ensure equal opportunities for higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.
“No Malaysian should be denied the opportunity to pursue higher education because of their background.
“We need to value every Malaysian’s human capital. Every Malaysian who achieves acceptable results should be given a place in a public university, in a public institution of higher learning. This should be the policy and spirit of the reforms that the Prime Minister is trying to bring,” he said in his policy speech at this year’s DAP congress.
Loke added that the party would also support any “proposal, formula or policy” by Anwar that could help reduce the people’s burden.
“We want to announce that DAP will support all these positive changes. We will give our support, but the most important thing is implementation and the firm decisions that need to be made by the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
“This is something I hope will send a strong message that whatever decisions are made by the DAP national congress today, what is most important is that we want to see positive changes in our country so that Malaysia becomes a progressive nation,” he said.
Yesterday, Anwar announced that the government would abolish AUKU, one of Pakatan Harapan’s long-standing reform commitments.

Title: Fadhlina tells PKR members not to wait for Parliament dissolution to prepare for polls
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek has urged party members to remain election-ready at all times and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved before making preparations.
She said the country’s political landscape was highly dynamic and could change at any time, including the possibility that parties currently in government would choose to negotiate with other political forces.
Fadhlina, who is the Education Minister, said PKR members must be prepared from now and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved or candidates to be announced, as they were politicians who knew what was happening around them.
“We must strengthen PKR so that whoever is with us, we remain strong. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong. We have the spirit.
“We have members who believe in the struggle, who are willing to knock on one door, then another, and then go down another street because they believe this country can change,” Fadhlina said in her winding-up speech at the PKR National Congress 2026 here today.
On the role of women in the party, Fadhlina said PKR must not merely rely on women as campaign workers, but instead provide them with greater opportunities to take on leadership roles.
“Involve them in decision-making, because if we want to convince society, particularly women, to vote for PKR, they too need to believe and see that the party truly believes in women’s leadership,” she said.
On governance, she said the party and government leadership must remain open to criticism, particularly when weaknesses were identified in decisions that had been made.
Fadhlina said the mandate given by the people must be used to do what was right, rather than merely pursuing popularity or taking the easy way out.
“I am not saying that all our decisions are always right. I am also not saying that we cannot be criticised.
“By all means, criticise us; there is no problem, this is our family. If something is not good enough, we improve it,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Control the media? We even give them massage chairs, Fahmi tells PKR congress
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today suggested that PKR will not resort to punitive measures against members of the press, even as some in the party believe its rivals are winning the messaging battle by fighting dirty.
Members of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) anchor party are gathered at this year’s national congress still reeling from the defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election, which coalition leaders blamed on the opposition’s identity-driven campaign, after PH was ousted following two terms in government.
Speaking to party delegates, Fahmi suggested that PKR had lost the communications war, leading voters to “vote over emotions instead of performance”.
Still, he said the coalition would not turn to harsher tactics to win the perception battle.
Fahmi said instead that his party was treating the press much better than previous governments, joking that it even provided massage chairs to reporters covering the party’s congress.
“Some in the party had asked me why not rein in the media (that help platform rivals’ messaging). Dear friends and comrades, let’s remind ourselves that we are born from the streets, from fighting the power that told the press to attack our president,” the PKR leader said.
“I was told by our friends in the press that it was worse before. They were even told what to write... but today we are so courteous when dealing with them... we even give them massage chairs. You can visit the media room to have a look yourself,” he added.
PH suffered a heavy defeat in the Negeri Sembilan state election after Barisan Nasional (BN) turned to Perikatan Nasional (PN) and succeeded in consolidating a large portion of the Malay vote.
Analysts said the shift in voter dynamics, including among Indian voters and lower turnout among Chinese voters, made it even tougher for the PKR-DAP-Amanah coalition.
The bloc won just 11 of the 36 state assembly seats, giving the BN-PN alliance a two-thirds majority. Two of PH’s heavyweights, former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun and senior minister Anthony Loke, were also among those defeated.
Fahmi appeared to have shouldered some of the blame for the party’s poor showing. He apologised on behalf of PKR’s central communications team and vowed to improve its strategy, particularly its messaging about the Anwar government’s economic performance.
The minister argued that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration had performed well economically, but there was a disconnect between the data and tangible results.
“The comms team would like to say it’s sorry and we will strive to change our strategy, so that the people would understand better what the (PH-led) government is doing and had done, hoping that if they can feel it in the stomach, then it may also nourish the heart,” he said.

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain, strong winds in Perlis, Melaka, Sarawak, other areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in the Peninsula and Sarawak until 1pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) through an alert at 8.35 am informed that the affected areas in the Peninsula include the entire states of Perlis and Melaka, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar in Kedah.
The weather warning also involves Kuantan, Pekan and Jerantut in Pahang; Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor; Port Dickson, Seremban, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negeri Sembilan; and Tangkak and Muar in Johor.
For Sarawak, the same forecast was issued for the areas of Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Maradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.
The warning is a short-term warning valid for a period not exceeding six hours for each advisory. — Bernama

Title: Rafizi: Bersama names 15 candidates early to give Melaka voters time to assess
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has announced candidates for 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka state legislative assembly, becoming the first party to unveil its candidates ahead of the state election,
The Star
reported.
The party’s line-up includes Dr Muhamad Solehin Saleh, 40, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who will contest Bemban.
Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said the early announcement was made before the state assembly is dissolved, allowing voters more time to assess the candidates and their plans.
“We are doing this before Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has even thought about dissolving the state assembly,” he was quoted as saying during the announcement in Melaka Baru last night.
Besides Bemban, Bersama will contest Kuala Linggi, Rembia, Gadek, Machap Jaya, Sungai Udang, Paya Rumput, Klebang, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana, Telok Mas and Serkam.
Rafizi, a former PKR deputy president, said the announcement marked the immediate start of the party’s campaign, with its candidates, members and volunteers expected to begin constituency-level work.
“Our campaign begins tonight. Go out and get to work,” he said.
He said announcing the candidates early would give voters sufficient time to assess their backgrounds, capabilities and plans, while allowing them to build relationships with local communities and understand issues affecting their constituencies.
Rafizi said a team was also preparing a manifesto and policy proposals specifically for Melaka voters.
He said Bersama planned to launch its manifesto during its first ceramah on nomination day.

Title: PAS wants Selangor to be launchpad for toppling PH, says Sanusi
Article:
TANJUNG KARANG, Aug 16 — PAS is targeting Selangor as the starting point for defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the state and subsequently at the federal level in the 16th general election, according to a report by
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT).
The report quoted Perikatan Nasional (PN) election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor as saying Selangor was a key target because of its importance as an economic powerhouse.
“If PH falls in Selangor, PH will fall at the federal level,” he was quoted as saying at a Selangor PAS election machinery gathering at the Selangor PAS complex here last night.
Sanusi, who is also Kedah Menteri Besar, urged voters to judge PH based on its record in government rather than its political messaging.
“Compare it with the performance of previous governments. What has PH achieved? They should show us what they have done while in power,” he said.
PH won 32 of Selangor’s 56 state seats in the 2023 state election, while PN won 22 and Barisan Nasional (BN) secured the remaining two.
PH and BN subsequently formed the state government.
FMT also reported that analysts had previously viewed closer cooperation between BN and PN as a potential challenge to PH’s position in Selangor, particularly if it resulted in greater consolidation of Malay votes.
Last month, Selangor PKR Youth deputy chief Shahrul Adnan called on the state PH leadership to reconsider its political cooperation with BN following BN-PN cooperation in the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan state election.

Title: Student loses RM29,000 after scammers pose as cops, threaten arrest over money laundering
Article:
IPOH, Aug 16  — Police arrested three local men, aged between 32 and 45, in five raids across Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Thursday for allegedly being involved in an online scam syndicate.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects were arrested at various locations in Petaling Jaya, Kelana Jaya, Ulu Kelang, Damansara and Kuala Lumpur.
He said the arrests followed a police report lodged by a 22-year-old student who lost RM28,999 after being deceived by individuals posing as law enforcement officers and claiming that he was involved in money laundering.
“The victim, a student at a higher education institution, received a call on July 31 from members of the syndicate posing as representatives of a delivery company, who claimed that a parcel containing illicit items had been addressed to him.
“The call was subsequently transferred to an individual posing as a law enforcement officer, who alleged that the victim was also involved in money laundering and intimidated him with threats of arrest and prosecution,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Alwi said the victim, fearing arrest, followed the syndicate’s instructions by transferring RM8,999 to several bank accounts and leaving gold jewellery worth about RM20,000 outside his house, after being promised that the money and jewellery would be returned once the investigation was concluded.
However, the victim realised he had been scammed when the items were not returned and subsequently lodged a police report on Aug 1.
Mohd Alwi said a team from the Commercial Crime Investigation Division of the Kampar District Police Headquarters subsequently gathered intelligence and tracked down members of the syndicate.
During the raids, police seized eight SIM Box units, 11 Starlink units, 509 SIM cards, a laptop, two routers and five mobile phones.
He said the equipment was believed to have been used as call gateways to manage communication traffic for online scam syndicates suspected of operating from abroad.
“All those arrested were remanded for four days until Monday to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak Merdeka Month programme with 214,095 student entries
Article:
IPOH, Aug 16 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today graced a programme to instil the spirit of loyalty to the Ruler and country in conjunction with the Perak-level 2026 Merdeka Month at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here last night.
Also in attendance were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, accompanied by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh.
Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar, in his royal address, said this year’s programme recorded an encouraging turnout, with 214,095 entries involving 83.6 per cent of primary and secondary school students in Perak.
He said this showed that the programme has not only received an overwhelming response but has also continued to grow as an important platform for discovering talent, building self-confidence and developing students’ potential in various fields contested.
“The 15 per cent increase in participation compared with the previous year also proves that the programme is gaining popularity and continues to be a significant platform.
“This programme certainly has a significant impact, not only physically but also on the thinking, values and future of the younger generation, in line with the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035,” he said.
He said the initiative is in line with the aspiration of nurturing a generation that excels not only academically but is also morally upright, thinks critically, is patriotic, appreciates the country’s history and heritage, and is capable of becoming credible leaders in the future.
At the event, Sultan Nazrin presented the special award for Best Achievement by District Education Office to the Kinta Utara District Education Office, which received RM20,000 in cash.
His Royal Highness also presented the prize for the champion of the upper secondary Malay Language Public Speaking Competition to Ifwat Arrafi Mohd Amin of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Abd Razak, Bagan Datuk, while E Johnnes Abysia from SMK Sungai Pari, Kinta Utara, won the English public speaking competition.
Sultan Nazrin also presented prizes for the choral speaking, choral recitation, choir and caricature drawing competitions for primary, lower secondary and upper secondary school categories, while Tuanku Zara presented prizes for the essay writing, poetry composition and poster drawing competitions for the same categories.
Their Royal Highnesses later toured the drawing and caricature exhibition before leaving the event. — Bernama

Title: ESSCom chief: Claims of armed men entering Semporna, Lahad Datu baseless
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Claims of a group of armed men entering Semporna and Lahad Datu, Sabah that went viral on social media are fake, Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said.
He also reassured that security in both areas was under control and the public need not be concerned about the claims.
“The viral claims are fake and we are aware of the photos uploaded on social media.
“Currently, the situation is under control and we are continuously monitoring to detect any threat or suspicious activity that can affect the safety of residents and the waters of East Sabah,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Victor said ESSCom always monitors and implements security control, especially in waters and strategic locations in the East Sabah Security Zone, adding that any information about security threats should be channelled to the authorities for further action and confirmation. — Bernama

Title: Police probe Facebook account owner over alleged seditious, insulting post against royals, govt
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 15 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is conducting an investigation into the owner of the Facebook account ‘Ahmad Mu’min’ following a post, which is suspected to contain elements of sedition and insult against the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the PDRM.
Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 is being conducted after a report was received from a 29-year-old man at 11.14 am yesterday.
“The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation according to legal procedures,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the latest post from the Facebook account owner, among other things, alleged that the police kicked a motorcyclist during a joint pperation at Pantai Penunjuk, Kijal, near here, at 6.30 pm yesterday.
“The allegation that the police kicked one of the motorcyclists is baseless and this can be seen through the recording that went viral on social media.
“The statement was malicious and the public is urged to verify the content of any post that has the potential to incite hatred against the police,” he said, adding that the operation was carried out following public complaints regarding illegal racing activities that disturb public order. — Bernama
